Hairs is a visualization technique for representing steady-state flow fields near or around contour surfaces, specifically addressing the failure of fiber bundles (or line bundles) when the flow vector points slightly into the surface [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that 'Hairs' is a visualization technique for representing steady-state flow fields near or around contour surfaces, specifically addressing the failure of fiber bundles (or line bundles) when the flow vector points slightly into the surface. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'We tried to use the fiber bundles to represent the flow around or near a surface. This broke down when the flow was slightly into the surface. A solution is to grow tiny hairs coming out of the surface.' Source [S2] confirms this with nearly identical wording, referring to 'line bundles' instead of 'fiber bundles'. Both sources confirm the technique is used for flow around/near surfaces and addresses the specific failure mode mentioned in the claim.
